records.text: A Mosshide Gnoll in the Wetlands snarls about fresh meat and bones to gnaw on when roused to fight.

A Mosshide mongrel of the Wetlands, counted among the growing gnoll population blamed for trampling fen plants and cutting too much wood. Its aggro barks crave fresh meat and bones; in combat it uses Spirit Decay.
A Mosshide Mistweaver in the Wetlands, speaking with the same hungry aggro snarls as its kin. It casts Frostbolt in combat and can summon a treasure horde while out of combat.
A Mosshide Fenrunner found across several parts of the Wetlands. It snarls about fresh meat and bones, uses Moss Hide in combat, and has a distinct aggro speech line.
A Mosshide Trapper of the Wetlands, whose aggro snarls hunger for fresh meat and bones. In combat it can cast a net, fitting its trapper role.
A Mosshide Brute is a hostile Mosshide combatant. On engaging a foe, it may snarl about fresh meat or bones to gnaw, giving its attack a predatory menace.
A Mosshide Mystic is a hostile Mosshide combatant whose aggro snarls match the Brute's: it threatens fresh meat and bones to gnaw. In combat, it can cast Lightning Bolt.
A Mosshide Alpha is a hostile Mosshide combatant. Like the Brute and Mystic, it snarls about fresh meat and bones to gnaw when engaging a foe; in combat it can use Battle Shout.

Bluegill Murlocs are a coastal people whose villages rise from the deep waters. Their raids threaten fishers and merchants along the Wetlands coast; this one is among the Bluegill encountered in that conflict and may flee for help when badly hurt.
A Bluegill Puddlejumper is one of the Bluegill found around the Wetlands. When badly hurt, it tries to flee and call for help.
A Bluegill Forager is found among the Bluegill in the Wetlands. In combat, it can cast Poison, giving this member of the group a dangerous attack.
A Bluegill Warrior is one of the Bluegill encountered around the Wetlands. It uses Battle Stance when out of combat.
A Bluegill Muckdweller is found in the Wetlands. In combat, it can use Gouge against its opponent.

A Bluegill Oracle is found among the Bluegill in the Wetlands. Its recorded behavior gives it a support role: it can place a Healing Ward and cast Healing Wave on an injured ally. When badly hurt, it may flee for help.
Black Slimes inhabit parts of the Wetlands. In combat, it attacks with Dark Sludge.
A Crimson Ooze is a hostile slime found in the wetlands. It attacks with Rancid Blood.
A Black Ooze is a hostile slime found across the wetlands. It attacks with Rancid Blood.
A Monstrous Ooze is a large hostile slime found in the wetlands. It attacks with Rancid Blood.
A Dragonmaw Raider is a hostile Dragonmaw clan combatant in the wetlands. It fights with a net and threatens its targets, proclaiming loyalty to the Dragonmaw.
A Dragonmaw Swamprunner serves as a Dragonmaw combatant in the wetlands. It uses poison and shares the raiders’ threats and declaration of loyalty; it also shouts on engaging an enemy.
A Dragonmaw Centurion is a Dragonmaw combatant in the wetlands. It uses Defensive Stance and shares the clan’s threats and declaration of loyalty.
A Dragonmaw battlemaster who fights for the clan. In combat, he threatens his opponents and calls for the Dragonmaw to prevail.
A Dragonmaw Shadowwarder who fights for the clan with shadow magic. His combat cries threaten his opponents and proclaim loyalty to the Dragonmaw.
A Fen Dweller, a local beast found across several Wetlands areas.

A Fen Creeper, a local beast found in several Wetlands areas. It can use Sneak while out of combat; the quest text describes these creatures as diseased, fevered growths in the marsh, but that account comes from their quest giver.
A Fen Lord of the Wetlands that can summon a Fen Dweller while out of combat.
A Red Whelp, a local creature found in several Wetlands areas. It uses Flame Lash in combat.
A young red dragon whelp found around the wetlands and nearby lowlands of the Eastern Kingdoms. It is an active combatant that uses Fireball when fighting.
A flamesnorting whelp encountered in the wetlands and nearby lowlands of the Eastern Kingdoms. It joins combat and uses Fireball.
A red dragonspawn encountered in the Eastern Kingdoms wetlands. This rank-and-file fighter attacks with Strike during combat.
A red wyrmkin encountered in the Eastern Kingdoms wetlands. It is a rank-and-file combatant that casts Fireball while fighting.
A red scalebane found in the Eastern Kingdoms wetlands. It serves as a rank-and-file fighter, using Cleave in combat.
A Scalebane lieutenant encountered in the Eastern Kingdoms wetlands, standing above the rank-and-file Scalebanes by title. It fights with Rend.
A Wyrmkin Firebrand is a combat creature found in the Wetlands. It attacks with Fireball Volley and Scorch.
A Scalebane Royal Guard is a combat creature found in the Wetlands. Its recorded attack is Fire Nova.

A Dark Iron Dwarf is one of the hostile dwarves fighting in the Wetlands. In combat, these dwarves threaten their opponent, boast of Dark Iron power, and may use Gift of Ragnaros. Motley Garmason’s call to kill Dark Iron Dwarves identifies them as targets in the conflict.

A Dark Iron Saboteur is one of the hostile dwarves fighting in the Wetlands. Its combat speech includes a threat to take its opponent down with it, and a dynamite-lighting cackle; it also uses Gift of Ragnaros. Motley Garmason’s call to kill saboteurs identifies them as targets in the conflict.

A Dark Iron Tunneler is one of the hostile dwarves fighting in the Wetlands. In combat, tunnelers threaten their opponent and boast of Dark Iron power; they may use Defensive Stance. Motley Garmason’s call to kill tunnelers identifies them as targets in the conflict.

A Dark Iron dwarf demolitionist serving the Dark Iron forces in the Wetlands, this combatant taunts its foes and threatens them in the name of the Dark Iron Dwarves. It uses bombs and fiery magic in battle.
A Dragonmaw clan bonewarder fighting in the Wetlands, this orc threatens to break an enemy’s bones and calls for the Dragonmaw’s victory. It weakens foes with curses and attacks with fire magic.
A crimson dragon whelp found in the Wetlands, this young dragon can protect itself with a fiery shield.

Longbraid the Grim commands the remnants of Dun Modr’s regiment after the Dark Iron attack killed many of his soldiers and his brother. He blames the Dark Iron for their losses and seeks to bring their leader, the warlock Balgaras the Foul, to justice. His harsh resolve reflects a commander still fighting to restore peace in the Wetlands.
A humanoid named Roggo Harlbarrow, found in the Wetlands.

Ashlan Stonesmirk is an explosives expert assigned to the regiment guarding Dun Modr and the Thandol Span. When presented with strange smelling powder, he identifies it as Seaforium and warns that wet Seaforium could destroy Ironforge. He explains how it can be defused and urges the finding to be reported to Chief Engineer Hinderweir.

Motley Garmason organizes the push against the Dark Iron forces that devastated the Thandol Span and Dun Modr, pressing for reinforcements as the campaign stalls. Bound by honor to stay with Longbraid, he sends others after Kam Deepfury, whom he regards as a conspirator responsible for Longbraid's family loss. He rejects Stormwind's handling of Deepfury and seeks vengeance for the attack.

Rhag Garmason is a besieged defender of Dun Modr and the Thandol Span, short on manpower and waiting for Ironforge reinforcements. When Ol' Rustlocke's scout report brings word of the scout's death and a cache of explosives arranged by Kam Deepfury, Rhag grieves, then turns the loss into a practical demand: destroy the cache before it can sever the northern supply line. He also asks for help finding Rustlocke and seeks additional Alliance soldiers to help reclaim the bridge and town.

Merrin Rockweaver is an Explorers' League member on the Whelgar excavation team. She and her companions uncovered artifacts and large bones before mottled raptors overwhelmed the site. In her account, Ormer bravely defended her and the prospector as they fled; many others died, and the team's work was ruined. Trapped at the site, Merrin entrusts a note about their plight to be carried to her husband, Tarrel, at Menethil Harbor.

Prospector Whelgar is an Explorers' League researcher at the excavation site, studying the Goaz Stone, whose translated text describes a “divine plan” and a “doomed prophecy.” With the invasion underway and beasts making the site dangerous, he admits he is too old to search for the four missing fragments himself and recruits help. Once the stone is restored, he continues translating its Titan script, finding a reference to Old Gods chained beneath the land. He remarks that Flagongut was bound to send someone for a fossil eventually.

Ormer Ironbraid says the raptors killed his fellow excavators and trapped him with Merrin and the Prospector. Bound to stay and protect the two survivors, he directs a three-stage revenge campaign, from killing the raptors to bringing Sarltooth to justice.
Leech Stalkers are common Wetlands leeches, aggressive beasts that use leech poison in combat.
The Leech Widow is a dangerous leech that attacks with deadly leech poison.
Razormaw Matriarch is a dangerous razormaw that fights with Rend Flesh and Fatal Bite. When badly hurt, it screeches to call for help.

A cursed sailor of the ill-fated Third Fleet, it is one of the dead crew said to remain trapped aboard their rotting ships. It threatens living strangers with joining the dead and mutters about brains, giving its threats a blunt, shambling menace.

A cursed marine of the ill-fated Third Fleet, it is one of the dead crew said to remain trapped aboard their rotting ships. Its aggro threats mirror the crew's grim welcome to the dead, while it also casts Curse of the Eye.

First Mate Snellig is a named member of the cursed crew, singled out alongside the sailors and marines in the account of the ill-fated Third Fleet. He uses the crew's threats to living intruders and casts Curse of the Eye; he can also use Disarm.

Captain Halyndor is remembered as the old captain of the doomed Intrepid, a ship of the cursed Third Fleet. The account of the crew's curse says he held authority over the ship's strongbox and its key. In combat he greets the living with the same dead crew's threats and casts Curse of the Eye.

Glorin Steelbrow helps search the Wetlands for precious Lightforge Iron, directing the search to the wreck of the Flying Osprey. He knows someone who can fashion it into a weapon against the necromancer threatening Duskwood. Glorin recognizes the Cursed Eye of Paleth but admits he cannot lift its curse, directing its bearer to Archbishop Benedictus and hoping the archbishop can help.

First Mate Fitzsimmons, sole surviving crewman of the Kul Tiras Third Fleet, lives with the fleet's loss and the curse trapping his dead shipmates aboard their wrecks. He turns to mead to steady himself and continue the tale, but his concern is for his “brothers”: he asks for their release and for the cursed object aboard the Intrepid to be retrieved and cleansed. He blames his former captain, Halyndor, for leading the fleet to its doom.

Karl Boran coordinates protection for Menethil's merchants, who are threatened by murlocs along the coast. He seeks the recovery of cargo taken from the merchant vessel Blind Princess, including a statuette of Terenas Menethil, and pays for completed contracts.

Rethiel the Greenwarden is a guardian of the Wetlands who measures the health of the land by its plants and creatures. Rethiel opposes the Mosshide gnolls' damage to bushes and trees, and sees reducing their numbers and the Fen Creepers as ways to restore balance. Rethiel speaks of roots and ferns and has many names, though visitors are invited to call the guardian Rethiel.

Gobbler is a bluegill murloc who harasses merchants along the road and retreats toward nearby murloc hovels. He prowls the river inlet north of Menethil Harbor; in combat he can use Pierce Armor and flee for assistance when badly hurt.

Sarltooth is a distinctive crocolisk at the Whelgar excavation site, singled out by Ormer Ironbraid as larger and more menacing than the other beasts. Ormer suspects it led the creatures disrupting the dig and calls for its death as justice.

Balgaras the Foul is a Dark Iron dwarf warlock who claims the Wetlands for his people and invokes Ragnaros against challengers. His combat taunts are contemptuous and boastful, dismissing opponents as weak fools and betrayers.
Wetlands Crocolisks are animals found across several parts of the Wetlands. This crocolisk is an adult.
Young Wetlands Crocolisks are found across several parts of the Wetlands.
Bluegill Raiders are humanoid opponents who fight with thrown weapons. They are encountered in several Wetlands areas.
Menethil Sentries are humanoid guards associated with Menethil. They are stationed at several sites in the Wetlands.
A humanoid named Thomas Booker, found in the Wetlands.
Brak Durnad is a weaponsmith who sells weapons and repairs equipment. His trade centers on arms and keeping them serviceable.
A humanoid named Jesse Halloran, found in the Wetlands.
A humanoid named Regina Halloran, found in the Wetlands.
A humanoid named Gimlok Rumdnul, found in the Wetlands.
Neal Allen sells engineering supplies, general goods, and ammunition.
Brahnmar is an armorer in the local area, offering goods to browse and repair service.
Camerick Jongleur is a wandering minstrel.
Gruham Rumdnul sells general supplies, including ammunition, in the local area.
Dewin Shimmerdawn is a local vendor of alchemy supplies.
Jennabink Powerseam offers tailoring supplies and specialty goods, with repair service also available.
Kersok Prond is identified as a tradesman and offers goods to browse in the local area.
Samor Festivus is a merchant titled Shady Dealer, offering goods for customers to browse.
Telurinon Moonshadow is Stormwind's herbalism trainer. He offers instruction in the craft to those who seek to learn it, a practical role reflected in his trainer's station.
Naela Trance is a bowyer and merchant specializing in bows.

Unger Statforth is a horse breeder who presents a steed as a lasting companion and credits years of careful breeding and care. Unger encourages buyers to choose thoughtfully, and explains that Stormwind’s trust is needed before doing business, to keep the finest horses from the kingdom’s enemies.
Murndan Derth is a gunsmith and merchant specializing in firearms.
Edwina Monzor is a fletcher and merchant specializing in arrows.
Falkan Armonis is a reagent supplier; customers can browse his goods through his shop.
Innkeeper Helbrek tends an inn where visitors can browse his goods or make the inn their home. He welcomes patrons to pull up a chair for a tankard and stories, with kegs to empty.

Hargin Mundar says his leg keeps him from taking on the gnolls, though he would like to clear them out. He warns that many adventurers have vanished in the marsh, recalls seeing a Sea Giant, and says sea spirits must be restless amid the stormy seas. Hiccups and burps break into his speech.
A humanoid named Timothy Clark, found in the Wetlands.
Caitlin Grassman is a humanoid in the Wetlands.
Bart Tidewater is identified as the captain of the Maiden's Virtue.
Andrea Halloran is a humanoid in the Wetlands.
Murphy West is a humanoid in the Wetlands.
Derina Rumdnul is a humanoid in the Wetlands.
Shellei Brondir is a gryphon master in Menethil Harbor. Travelers can ask about flight destinations; the service dialogue asks where they would like to fly.

Valstag Ironjaw directs the response to Dragonmaw activity around Algaz from Menethil Harbor. He sends travelers through Dun Algaz to fight Dragonmaw scouts and grunts, then receives reports from those returning from Loch Modan. The clan’s sudden move into Algaz remains unexplained to him.
The Giant Wetlands Crocolisk is a large Wetlands creature found in several local areas. It attacks with Tendon Rip when combat begins.

Ma'ruk Wyrmscale is a Dragonmaw warlord and lieutenant. A scout's report describes him as sent to organize orcs in Algaz and cut off the land route to Menethil Harbor; he is headquartered in a cave between the tunnels.

Chieftain Nek'rosh leads the Dragonmaw and declares his allegiance in battle. His threats are blunt and brutal, promising to break an opponent's bones beneath his boot. His battle cries frame a fight as service to the Dragonmaw.

Einar Stonegrip is a hunter who supplies crocolisk skins to Menethil Harbor tanner James Halloran. He asks travelers heading toward Menethil to deliver a bundle for him, explaining that he is putting off facing his wife, who is in a bad mood.

James Halloran is a Menethil Harbor tanner whose cured crocolisk skins are shipped to ports around the world. Hunter Einar supplies him, and Halloran knows Einar has lately sent his skins by messenger. After a crocolisk attack leaves his apprentice gravely injured, Halloran calls him like a son and worries about his future. He continues seeking skins for his trade.

Tarrel Rockweaver waits anxiously for news of his wife, Merrin, a member of the Whelgar Excavation team. After her letters stop arriving, he asks a scout to check on the dig. Merrin's note reports that Mottled Raptors attacked, leaving her and others trapped amid the ruined excavation; Tarrel grieves the losses and hopes for a day when King Magni's subjects can live without fear.

A wounded survivor of Dun Modr's regiment, Harlo Barnaby recalls the Dark Iron attack after the Thandol Span ambush. He was struck by an axe during the retreat and awoke in Menethil Harbor, fearing for his fellow soldiers. Harlo holds out hope that their leader, Longbraid, survived and asks that he be sought near Dun Modr.
A ram that may flee for help when wounded.
A crewman of the Maiden's Virtue.
A Dragonmaw grunt who threatens opponents and calls for the Dragonmaw's victory in battle.
A Dragonmaw Scout of the clan's force at Dun Algaz, it threatens opponents in battle and calls for the Dragonmaw to prevail. Its words express the clan's shared fighting spirit.

Captain Stoutfist directs Menethil's defense against the Dragonmaw. He sends allies to strike their encampment, recover its banners, and destroy catapults before Nek'rosh can besiege the harbor while Dun Algaz blocks reinforcements. He recounts how Nekros's control of the red dragons failed, leading to his death, and that Nek'rosh seeks revenge on the dragons. Stoutfist recognizes reports of prior success and urges continued service to Ironforge.
Garneg Charskull is an elite Dragonmaw fighter who uses Flame Shock, threatens opponents in combat, and calls for the Dragonmaw to prevail. His fighting cries express the clan's shared spirit.

Sida recounts being attacked by oozes during her weekly visit to Ironbeard's Tomb. She threw her bag at one while escaping and is anxious to recover its contents; when it is returned, she quickly empties it and offers it to the finder.
Terl Arakor is fiercely protective of his wagon, emphatically insisting that it belongs to him.
Mountaineer Grugelm is a mountaineer.
Mountaineer Thar is a mountaineer.
Mountaineer Rharen is a mountaineer.
Wenna Silkbeard is a special goods dealer who offers goods and repairs.
Fradd Swiftgear is an engineering-supplies merchant in Menethil Harbor, where he offers goods to browse.

Archaeologist Flagongut is an Explorers’ League archaeologist whose research centers on fossils and the Stone of Relu. He believes the stone can unlock the fossils’ hidden power; after losing it to raptors while traveling to meet Prospector Whelgar, he seeks the relic and Whelgar’s original fossil. When presented with Remtravel’s fossil, he recognizes its resemblance to one he saw at an Explorers’ League conference. His work joins archaeological mystery to the League’s hopes for the future, and he proceeds to study the artifacts together.
Stuart Fleming is a fishing-supplies merchant in Menethil Harbor, offering goods to browse.

Harold Riggs is a fishing trainer. His guidance points anglers who have outgrown his skill toward further learning: Old Man Heming’s book “The Bass and You” in Booty Bay, or Nat Pagle in Dustwallow Marsh. The advice reflects the trainee’s current skill and does not establish when either option is available.
The Dark Iron Entrepreneur is a speciality-goods merchant who offers goods to browse.

Fremal Doohickey trains first aid and recommends Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen in Theramore for further training. Fremal has heard that Deneb Walker in Stromgarde has a book to improve first-aid techniques.
Junder Brokk is a humanoid in the Wetlands.
Cave Stalkers are beasts that use Leech Poison in combat.
Red Jack Flint is a humanoid found in Wetlands.

Tapoke “Slim” Jahn admits getting Hendel aboard the king of Stormwind’s ship for the Defias, declaring that they did not pay enough to die for their cause. Tapoke claims the Defias worked with another party but professes no further knowledge. Boasts about not being alone give way to a willingness to talk rather than face violence.

Mikhail is a retired Stormwind underground contact who now tends the bar in Menethil. He keeps Elling’s investigation discreet, shares what he knows about Slim and the missing diplomat, and helps trace Hendel through his tavern’s regulars. Though he says he misses the excitement of his former work, he does not want Elling to draw him back to Stormwind.

Vincent Hyal works in Menethil Harbor and speaks with pride and affection about his brother James, a fine cook who taught him much of what he knows. James left to join Jaina Proudmoore across the sea, later setting up an inn; Vincent believes he is doing well but has not heard from him in some time. He asks after James through a contact in Theramore.
A black stallion.
Pinto is a beast associated with a questgiver role, though the supplied records do not identify the quest or its subject.
Comar Villard remains faithful to his lost love and wanders the Wetlands hoping to find his wife.
A Dark Iron combatant who fights with a rifle and invokes Dark Iron identity, warning enemies not to cross the clan and threatening them with death.
Kixxle is a vendor specializing in potions and herbs.
A riding ram, represented in the native creature data as an animal creature.
Bethaine Flinthammer is a stable master who handles pet stabling and lost-companion recovery.
Chestnut Mare is a chestnut-coated horse, identified by her coloring and by the name mare.
Brown Horse is a brown-coated horse, a clear example of the ordinary horses found across Azeroth.

Adam Lind is an Alliance guide at a dock in the Wetlands. He points travelers toward passage to Theramore and warns that travel through those lands is rarely safe for Alliance people, urging them to watch their step and their backs.
Axtroz is a drake champion and lieutenant of the Red Flight at Grim Batol. His enemies seek his destruction; in combat he uses Flame Breath, Vicious Rend, and Fireball.
Dwarven Farmer is a dwarf whose role is farm work, defined by practical agricultural labor.
Mirelow is a rare elemental that uses Entangling Roots in combat, binding opponents in place.
Gnawbone is a powerful creature that attacks with Rend and may flee for help when badly wounded.
Sludginn is a formidable creature whose combat relies on Dark Sludge and Leech Poison.

The Wetlands Flame Warden tends an Alliance festival fire. It urges visitors to honor Alliance flames and desecrate the Horde's, whose efforts it calls unworthy, and reminds them that Alliance fires burn in every land with an Alliance settlement.
Ludin Farrow is a dockmaster who points travelers bound for Northrend to the icebreaker Northspear, which sails from here to Valgarde in the Howling Fjord.

place_records.text: You are in Wetlands, Eastern Kingdoms land held in places by the Alliance, with no settlement of the other side. Menethil Harbor and Sundown Marsh are its main settlements. Mosshide gnolls, crocolisks and mottled raptors haunt its fens and marshes, murlocs threaten Menethil's merchants along the coast, and Dark Iron dwarves have overrun Dun Modr.

You are in Whelgar's Excavation Site, a dig in the Wetlands run by Explorers' League researchers. Mottled raptors overran it after the team uncovered large bones, and Ormer Ironbraid, who is bound to protect the survivors Merrin Rockweaver and Prospector Whelgar, vows revenge on the raptors. Mottled Scytheclaws, Mottled Razormaws and a raptor named Sarltooth, whom Ormer suspects led the attack, still prowl the site.

You are in Menethil Harbor, the Alliance harbor of the Wetlands, with its inn and flight master. Tanner James Halloran ships cured crocolisk skins to ports around the world, while Karl Boran coordinates protection for the merchants threatened by murlocs along the coast. Captain Stoutfist directs the harbor's defense against the Dragonmaw, and bluegill raiders and young crocolisks still lurk nearby.

You are in Dun Modr, an Alliance hold in the Wetlands. Longbraid the Grim commands what remains of its regiment, while Rhag Garmason holds the defenses and waits for Ironforge reinforcements. Dark Iron tunnelers, saboteurs and demolitionists are the dangers here.

You are in Baradin Bay, a bay in the Wetlands where the dockmaster Ludin Farrow points travelers bound for Northrend to the icebreaker Northspear, which sails to Valgarde in the Howling Fjord. Murlocs and giant crocolisks lurk in the water. Adam Lind, a guide at the dock, warns that the way to Theramore is rarely safe for Alliance people.

You are in Menethil Bay, a stretch of water in the Wetlands where bluegill raiders, Wetlands crocolisks and young crocolisks hunt. Murlocs have stolen the rest of the Lightforge Ingots from a waterlogged chest near the Flying Osprey wreck, and Glorin Steelbrow is searching the Wetlands for more Lightforge iron.

You are in Ironbeard's Tomb, northeast of Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Black oozes, monstrous oozes and crimson oozes are the dangers here, and one ooze swallowed a visitor's bag whole. Highland raptors and fen creepers lurk nearby.

You are in Dun Algaz, where four Alliance mountaineers stand against the Dragonmaw. Dragonmaw scouts and grunts gather here, and Ma'ruk Wyrmscale is a notable threat. Valstag Ironjaw in Menethil Harbor directs the response to Dragonmaw activity around Algaz.

You are in Thandol Span, a bridge in the Wetlands that Dark Iron forces devastated. Dark Iron saboteurs still lurk around it. Comar Villard roams this area, faithful to his lost love and hoping to find his wife.

You are in Direforge Hill, southeast of Dun Modr in the Wetlands. Balgaras the Foul, the warlock who leads the Dark Iron here, hides in his camp on the hill. Dark Iron dwarves, tunnelers and saboteurs share the slopes with highland lashtails, crimson whelps and highland scytheclaws.

You are in Raptor Ridge, a ridge in the Wetlands where highland razormaws and elder razormaws are the dangers. A spirit healer here offers a return to the living for a price, while cautioning that it may not yet be the traveler's time.
You are in Black Channel Marsh, a marsh in the Wetlands where mottled raptors and mottled screechers hunt among young crocolisks, fen dwellers and black oozes.
You are in Mosshide Fen, a fen in the Wetlands where mosshide gnolls, mongrels and fenrunners roam among young crocolisks, black slimes and fen dwellers.
You are in Thelgen Rock, part of the Wetlands. Leech Stalkers and Black Slimes are the dangers here.

You are in Bluegill Marsh, part of the Wetlands, where Bluegill murlocs swarm the hovels. Mirelow is also a danger here. Searches for the lost Menethil Statuette are still going on among the murloc hovels.
You are in Saltspray Glen, part of the Wetlands. Wetlands crocolisks, highland lashtails, highland scytheclaws and highland razormaws roam it, and fen creepers and fen lords lurk among them.

You are in Sundown Marsh, a part of the Wetlands held by the Alliance. Wenna Silkbeard deals in special goods here, and Fradd Swiftgear in engineering supplies. A spirit healer is on hand for the dead, and mosshide trappers, brutes and crocolisks roam the marsh.

You are in The Green Belt, part of the Wetlands where Rethiel the Greenwarden watches over the plants and creatures. Rethiel is opposed to the mosshide gnolls, who cut the trees for their fires, and to the fen creepers that have risen as diseased blisters on the land. Whelps and highland raptors roam the area.
You are in Angerfang Encampment, a Dragonmaw camp in the Wetlands. Dragonmaw raiders, bonewarders, swamprunners and centurions fill it, and Chieftain Nek'rosh is still at large here.
You are in Dragonmaw Gates, a place in the Wetlands where Scalebane royal guards, Wyrmkin firebrands and red dragonspawn are found in numbers.

You are in The Lost Fleet, an area of the Wetlands haunted by Cursed Marines and Cursed Sailors, with Captain Halyndor among them. A cursed Eye of Paleth was found in a chest here, and its curse is not yet removed.
